Petitioner/s by Sri.Puttaswamy.H., Advocate Respondent No.1 by M.R. Mamatha, Advocate Respondent No.2 is placed exparte ===
Date of filing of petition : 28.12.2021 ===
 M.V.C.No.5826/2021  3 SCCH - 7  :JUDGMENT:

1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 25.10.2021.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 25.10.2021 at about 900 a.m., he was riding Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle bearing registration No.KA04KB7078 after dropping his children at Government School Honaganahatti, Tavarekere while returning towards his residence slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road near Baichaguppe Cross, Bangalore Magadi Road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bangalore city at that time the driver of Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25 C4990 drove the same from opposite direction in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and came to the extreme wrong side of M.V.C.No.5826/2021 4 SCCH - 7 the road and dashed against his Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle and due to impact he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Smt. Jayadevi Memorial Hospital, Chikkagollarahatti,
Magadi Main Road, Bangalore wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and aged about 44 years and he was doing animal Husbandary and earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident he became permanently disabled.

M.V.C.No.5826/202 vs Petitioner/S By Sri.Puttaswamy.H on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75420320/
2

This accident is took place due to the negligence of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C4990 as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, he prayed to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared through their counsel and filed their written statement and the respondent No.2 is placed exparte.
The respondent No.1  insurer denied the entire contentions of the petitioner.

Further the respondent No.1 admitted that they have issued the Insurance Policy to the Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C4990 and their liability is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

The respondent No.1 contended that as on the date of the accident the driver of the said Bus was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle involved in the accident hence it is violation of terms and conditions of the policy as such there are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent No.1 has prayed for dismissal of claim petition.
5. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.
M.V.C.No.5826/2021 6 SCCH - 7 :: I S S U E S ::

(1) Whether petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C 4990 and as a result he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioner prove the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

(4) What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case of petitioner, petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to P.12 M.V.C.No.5826/2021 7 SCCH - 7 and doctor got examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.13 and Ex.P.14 and closed their side.
The respondents are not adduced any evidence.
7. Heard the arguments of both side.

8. My findings to the above referred Issues are as under;
 Issue No.1 : In the affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative M.V.C.No.5826/202 vs Petitioner/S By Sri.Puttaswamy.H on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75420320/
3  Issue No.3 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order,
 for the following.......
 :REASONS:
9. Issue No.1: The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in his examination in chief he deposed as per the contentions taken by him and got marked FIR as per Ex.P 1, Complaint as per Ex.P2,
spot mahazar as per Ex.P.3, Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.4 and Charge Sheet as per Ex.P.5.

By perusing these documents it is clearly goes to M.V.C.No.5826/2021 8 SCCH - 7 show that this accident was took place due to the negligence on the part of driver of Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C4990.

Further in the cross examination of PW.1, he clearly deposed that from 6 - 7 years he is riding the motorcycle and he is having driving licence to ride the motorcycle and he has not produced the same.
He deposed that when he was proceeding in a motorcycle from his back side the Bus dashed against his motorcycle and caused this accident.
He deposed that his wife has admitted him to the Hospital.
He denied that he himself dashed to the Bus hence he has not produced the IMV Report.
10. In the crossexamination of PW.1 nothing worth is brought on record to show that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C 4990.

Further by perusing Charge Sheet marked as per Ex.P.5 it goes to shows that the police after M.V.C.No.5826/2021 9 SCCH - 7 completion of the investigation has came to conclusion that due to the negligence of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C4990 this accident was took place and filed Charge Sheet against the driver of the said Bus.

Hence by looking to the entire oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner it is clear that this accident is occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA 25C4990.
Further by perusing the Wound Certificate marked as per Ex.P.4 clearly goes to shows that in this accident the petitioner has sustained injuries as stated in his petition.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:

The petitioner contended that as on the date of accident he was aged about 44 years and he was doing Animal Husbandry and thereby earning Rs.30,000/ p.m. M.V.C.No.5826/2021 10 SCCH - 7 Due to the injuries sustained in the accident he became permanently disabled.
12. In order to prove the age of the petitioner, he relied on the Adhar Card marked as per Ex.P.9 wherein the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 01.01.1977.
Hence, the age of petitioner is considered at 44 years as on the date of accident.
13. So for as income of the petitioner is concern the petitioner contended that he was working doing Animal Husbandry and thereby earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.
In support of this contention the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he was earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.

Hence in the absence of the acceptable material with regard to the income, by considering the occupation, age the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/ p.m., and the occupation of the M.V.C.No.5826/202 vs Petitioner/S By Sri.Puttaswamy.H

on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75420320/
4 petitioner is considered as Animal M.V.C.No.5826/2021 11 SCCH - 7 Husbandry.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:

The petitioner contended that in the accident he has sustained fracture of both bones right leg, fracture of proximal phalanx right ring finger and laceration over right foot and due to the injuries he is not in a position to do any work and he is permanently disabled.
In support of this contention the petitioner has got examined Dr.Arjun S. Prakash as PW.2.

The PW.2 deposed that in the RTA occurred on 25.10.2021 the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bones right leg,
fracture of proximal phalanx right ring finger and laceration over right foot and the petitioner undergone reduction and Kwiring for injury and he was on regular follow up with him and was advised physiotherapy for stiffness of knee and ankle and he recently examined petitioner for disability assessment and M.V.C.No.5826/2021 12 SCCH - 7 he found that complete union of all fractures, stiffness of right knee and stiffness of right ankle and petitioner complains of pain in right knee.

Further deposed that the petitioner has sustained permanent physical disability for whole body at 16% and the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implants which will cost approximately Rs.45,000/.
The Doctor has produced Case Sheet as per Ex.P.13 and Xray film as per Ex.P.14.
In the crossexamination he deposed that he personally given treatment to the petitioner and he is one the team member who are treated the petitioner.
Further deposed that now the fracture are united and he has not produced the clinical notes.
He deposed that he has not advised for physiotherapy treatment after assessing the disability.
He denied that to help the petitioner he has assessed the disability on the higher side.
He deposed that he has not issued any estimation for removal of implants and for M.V.C.No.5826/2021 13 SCCH - 7 removal of implants the petitioner needs Rs.45,000/.
He denied that he is deposing falsely.
15. From the evidence of PW.2 it is clear that the doctor has not given functional disability of the petitioner.

As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as Animal Husbandry due to the injuries sustained in the accident now it is difficult for the petitioner to stand for long time, lift the heavy weight and milk the cows.

Hence by considering the age, nature of injury and also relying on the authority reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 12% to the whole body.
16. With regard to the quantum, the age of the petitioner is considered as 44 years and the income is considered at Rs.15,000/ p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 14 is applicable and functional disability is considered at M.V.C.No.5826/2021 14 SCCH - 7 12%.
On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner, the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs.15,000/ X 12 X 14 X 12/100) = Rs.3,02,400/.
Hence, an amount of Rs.3,02,400/ is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the permanent disability suffered by him in the accident.

17. No doubt in the accident the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bones right leg, fracture of proximal phalanx right ring finger and laceration over right foot and the petitioner has undergone surgery which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered some pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.50,000/ is awarded towards pain and sufferings.
M.V.C.No.5826/202 vs Petitioner/S

By Sri.Puttaswamy.H on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75420320/
5 18.

Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner might have taken rest for at least for a period of one month and during this period he might have taken M.V.C.No.5826/2021 15 SCCH - 7 nutritious food and taken assistance of an attendant hence an amount of Rs.25,000/ is awarded under the head of loss of earning during the period of treatment, rest, nourishment and attendant charges.
Further the petitioner has produced the hospital and medicine bills as per Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.10 for an amount of Rs.1,53,674/.
Hence an amount of Rs.1,53,674/ is awarded to the petitioner under the head of hospital and medicine charges.
19. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.25,000/ is awarded towards loss of amenities.
Further from the evidence of PW.2 and Xrays marked as per Ex.P.14 it goes to shows that still the implants are not removed and for removal of implants the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery.
Hence an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under the future medical expenses.

Hence, The M.V.C.No.5826/2021 16 SCCH - 7 petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads;
Towards loss of future income Rs. 3,02,400.00
Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000.00

Towards medicine and hospital Rs. 1,53,674.00 bill Towards loss of earning during Rs. 25,000.00 rest period and attendant charges Towards loss of amenities Rs. 25,000.00 Future medical expenses Rs.
20,000.00 Total Rs. 5,76,074.00 Hence the petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable compensation amount of Rs.5,76,074/.
20.
While answering the issue No.1 this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that, accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C4990.
The petitioner contended that the respondent No.1 is the insurer and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the said vehicle hence they are jointly ans severally liable to pay compensation to him.

As the policy M.V.C.No.5826/2021 17 SCCH - 7 issued to the Bus was in force and there is no violation of terms and conditions of the policy as such the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C4990 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a from the date of petition.
Hence, I answered the issue No.3 in partly affirmative.

21. Issue No.4: For the above stated reasons I proceed to pass the following;
:ORDER:
Claim petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of Rs.1,000/.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.5,76,074/ (Rupees Five Lakh Seventy Six Thousand Seventy Four Only) with interest at the M.V.C.No.5826/2021 18 SCCH - 7 rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.
M.V.C.No.5826/202 vs Petitioner/S By Sri.Puttaswamy.H on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75420320/
6

The respondent No.1 being insurer of Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C4990 is directed to deposit the awarded compensation amount in the Court within 02 month from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.

:APPORTIONMENT:
On deposit of compensation amount the petitioner shall deposit 50% of the compensation amount in any of the Nationalized Banks as F.D. for a period of 3 years.

After expiry of period of fixed deposit the Bank Authorities are at liberty to release the amount shown in the F.D. to the concerned depositor in accordance with rules M.V.C.No.5826/2021 19 SCCH - 7 and regulations of the bank after proper identification of the depositor.
Remaining 50% amount is to be paid to Injured/Petitioner under Epayment and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court.

As the policy M.V.C.No.5826/2021 17 SCCH - 7 issued to the Bus was in force and there is no violation of terms and conditions of the policy as such the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C4990 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a from the date of petition.
Hence, I answered the issue No.3 in partly affirmative.

21. Issue No.4: For the above stated reasons I proceed to pass the following;
:ORDER:
Claim petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of Rs.1,000/.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.5,76,074/ (Rupees Five Lakh Seventy Six Thousand Seventy Four Only) with interest at the M.V.C.No.5826/2021 18 SCCH - 7 rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.

6

The respondent No.1 being insurer of Ashok Leyland Bus bearing registration No.KA25C4990 is directed to deposit the awarded compensation amount in the Court within 02 month from the date of this judgment.

:APPORTIONMENT:
On deposit of compensation amount the petitioner shall deposit 50% of the compensation amount in any of the Nationalized Banks as F.D. for a period of 3 years.

After expiry of period of fixed deposit the Bank Authorities are at liberty to release the amount shown in the F.D. to the concerned depositor in accordance with rules M.V.C.No.5826/2021 19 SCCH - 7 and regulations of the bank after proper identification of the depositor.
Remaining 50% amount is to be paid to Injured/Petitioner under Epayment and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court.
